issue.title: Stop the upload foreground service from crashing the app [Returning online and sync changes Audit]
issue.body:
Found during the returning online and synchronizing changes audit (#530, epic #526).

**Severity:** High  
**Launch blocker:** To be decided with product  
**Confirmed on:** Xiaomi Redmi Note 9 Pro, Android 10 (API 29), local debug build of `09ff2fd` (PR #559 head), `dev.api.fluent.bible` (scenarios B.6, B.7, B.8, C.10)

## Summary

Uploading takes after reconnecting crashes the app with `RemoteServiceException: Context.startForegroundService() did not then call Service.startForeground()` (`UploadSyncForegroundService`).

Every notification `start` and `update` calls `startForegroundService()` (`modules/upload-sync-foreground/android/src/main/java/expo/modules/uploadsyncforeground/UploadSyncForegroundModule.kt:14-36`), and the JS clears it on each `complete` / `idle` event (`src/services/uploadProgressNotification.ts:25-41`). The worker emits `complete` after every chapter (`src/services/recordingSync.ts:382`), and one reconnect starts several concurrent sessions: `runSession` guards on `sessionPromise` (`src/services/uploadOrchestratorCore.ts:131`) but only sets it at `:220`, after two awaits (`:143`, `:170`), and `evaluateAuto` does not await it (`:263-264`). The `:143` await is new in PR #559 (a `/health` probe of up to 5 s) and widens the window. `stopService()` then runs before the service calls `startForeground()`, and Android kills the app.

## Expected

One persistent upload notification per session (#152); the app never crashes because of it.

## Actual

The app crashes (red box on the debug build; the app just closes on others). The 2026-09-28 device log shows five "Upload session started" entries for one chapter within 300 ms and five notification start/clear pairs within 200 ms. The device crash buffer holds the same exception on 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-21, before PR #559.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In airplane mode, record takes in 2 or more chapters.
2. Turn Wi-Fi back on and open the Sync page (or background the app).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One reconnect starts at most one upload session (the in-flight guard is set before any await).
- [ ] The foreground service is started once per session and stopped only on complete, pause or cancel; a stop never races a pending start.
- [ ] Unit tests: concurrent connectivity events start one session; the notification event stream for a multi-chapter session produces one show and one clear.
- [ ] Android device QA: reconnect with pending takes in several chapters, foreground and background, with no crash.

## Related

- Parent audit: #530 (epic #526)
- #152, #150, #559; progress counts from the same event stream: #600
- Assessment: `docs/assessments/returning-online-and-sync/README.md` (PR #598)

comments.body:
Reproduced during the offline chapter assignment audit (#533) with a single chapter.

**Confirmed on:** Xiaomi Redmi Note 9 Pro, Android 10 (API 29), local debug build of `main` @ `fb634e5` (without PR #559), `dev.api.fluent.bible` (2026-09-28 16:57, Acts 6).

- One offline take on one chapter; turning Wi-Fi on started **two** automatic upload sessions 2 ms apart (16:57:41.638 and .640), with notification start/clear pairs within 2 ms.
- The app then crashed with `RemoteServiceException: Context.startForegroundService() did not then call Service.startForeground()` (`UploadSyncForegroundService`) at 16:57:43.
- Duplicate sessions per trigger were seen again on 2026-09-29 (Sync Now at 08:03 started three sessions; the reconnect at 12:02 started two).

So the crash does not need many chapters; a duplicate session on one reconnect is enough.

Assessment: `docs/assessments/offline-chapter-assignment/README.md` (PR #609).
